##2) When to use which method?

| Need | Typical method | Main asset | Main limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| High quality all-rounder | Focus stacking | Strong visual result | Multiple acquisition |
| Fast depth with few holds | Depth from defocus | 2 images are enough | Limited local accuracy |
| Finer depth | Confocal stereo | High granularity | More complex setup |
| Post-capture refocus | Light field | Flexibility after setting | Reduced spatial resolution |
| Depth + deblurring on an image | Coded opening | Compact system | Model/Texture Aware |
| Stable deblurring on depth range | Wavefront coding | Quasi-invariant PSF | Specialized optics |

---

##3) “Inverse problem” reasoning

### Model

- Describe image formation (convolution, PSF, noise).

### Regularize

- Introduce plausible constraints (priors on gradients/textures/depth).

### Infer

- Optimize or estimate hidden variables (sharp image, depth).

### To validate

- Evaluate on texture, edges, uniform areas, robustness to noise.

---

##4) Mini Exam Scenarios

### Scenario A - Product macro in e-commerce

- Objective: sharp image (entire object).
- Recommended choice: focus stacking.
- Justification: strong requirement for overall clarity.

### Scenario B - Constrained budget mobile robot

- Objective: depth from a single camera.
- Possible choice: coded opening.
- Justification: cost/complexity compromise with depth + sharp image.

### Scenario C - Creative camera for post-production

- Objective: change the focus after capture.
- Recommended choice: plenoptic camera.
- Justification: digital refocusing and virtual views.

---

##5) Mathematical points to know how to explain

- Thin lens: $1/f = 1/D + 1/D'$.
- Merge focus stack: $I_{fused} = (\sum w_k I_k)/(\sum w_k)$.
- Degradation: $y = f \otimes x + n$.
- Regularized deconvolution: $\hat{x}=\arg\min \|f\otimes x-y\|^2 + \lambda P(\nabla x)$.

##6) Flash Questions

- Why does focal flow often fail on poorly textured areas?
- Why does a coded aperture help depth discrimination?
- What is the central compromise of plenoptic cameras?
- In which case is a quasi-invariant PSF decisive?

---

##7) Checklist before exam

- I know how to compare the 4 depth methods.
- I know how to explain the spatial/angular compromise of the light field.
- I know how to explain the frequency logic of the coded opening.
- I know how to distinguish coded aperture, wavefront coding and lattice lens.

---

##8) Common Mistakes

- Believing that a single method is optimal everywhere.
- Forgetting alignment in focus stacking.
- Confusing digital refocusing and deconvolution.
- Forget that the local texture strongly conditions the depth quality.
